user.title: Connect Jev Home Assistant Sentinel
user.description: Choose one of four modes. Both sides answer with a System One decision model, also written a typed decision model: one that returns typed values with a probability for each rather than prose. api_with_local_fallback calls the hosted API first and the local model if it fails. api_only calls the hosted API alone. local_only calls the local model alone. local_with_api_fallback calls the local model first and the hosted API if it fails. Names from earlier versions still work and mean the same thing: jev_api and clef_api are api_only, laya_local is local_only, and laya_with_jev_fallback and clef_with_jev_fallback are local_with_api_fallback. local_model selects which local System One decision model answers, so Laya or another pre-deterministic routing model fits without a code change. The hosted API side is Jev over the OpenRouter API key, or Cloudflare Clef, which reads its Workers AI account and API token from the CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variables; this form does not ask for them because a config entry is stored on disk in plain text.

data.laya_model: Local checkpoint (deprecated, superseded by Local System One decision model)

error.api_key_required: The modes that reach the hosted API need an OpenRouter API key. Select local_only only when a local decision-model server is running, or Clef when CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID are set in the environment.
error.local_model_invalid: The local System One decision model name cannot be empty and cannot contain whitespace, a quote, a backslash, or the URL characters ?, #, and &. Use laya, or the engine name of any other local pre-deterministic routing model you run.
